chunks: And with the foregoing chain of narration from Ali ibn Mahzyar, from Ibn Abi Najran, from al-Hasan ibn Bahr, from Furat ibn Ahnaf, from a man among the companions of the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib, may the blessings of God be upon him, who said: I heard him saying:
Be humble and inconspicuous, and do not seek fame. Conceal yourself so that you are neither mentioned nor known. Guard your secret, maintain silence, and you will remain safe.
Then he pointed with his hand toward his chest, saying: You will please the righteous and enrage the wicked. And he pointed with his hand toward the general public.

key_terms.تبذل: To be humble, to live simply among common people
key_terms.تشهر: To become famous, to seek public notoriety

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about avoiding fame and seeking humility?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) counsels his followers to live in humility and obscurity, avoiding fame and public attention. This teaching, delivered in his circle of companions in Kufa, reflects the Shia emphasis on spiritual sincerity over outward recognition — the one who guards inner piety (pointing to his chest) will be a source of joy for the righteous and frustration for the wicked.
word_analysis: and with the chain of narration
